cover_sub: Explore the financial health data shaping the nonprofit landscape.

slides.label: Overview
slides.headline: Operating Reserves Across Nonprofits
slides.body: Approximately 40% of nonprofits maintain fewer than three months of operating reserves, a critical factor for sustainability.

slides.label: Small Organizations
slides.headline: Small Nonprofits' Financial Profiles
slides.body: Organizations under $500K often invest directly in programs, resulting in leaner reserves, though not necessarily indicative of struggle.

slides.label: Funding Trends
slides.headline: Funding Decline Amid Growth
slides.body: Despite increasing numbers, the average funding per nonprofit has decreased by 3%, highlighting the funding paradox.

slides.label: Vulnerability
slides.headline: Vulnerability of Small Organizations
slides.body: Small nonprofits are particularly vulnerable to financial pressures, as they often operate with limited reserves and resources.

slides.label: Data Insight
slides.headline: The Role of Data in Nonprofit Funding
slides.body: Funders lack comprehensive data to identify where capital can have the most significant impact, making strategic support challenging.

slides.label: Impact
slides.headline: The Importance of Informed Giving
slides.body: Understanding financial health data can guide more effective and impactful funding decisions, supporting nonprofits' missions.
